label: Length-9 sequences: <DEL> step and last ~3 copy steps (weak, sparse)
explanation: Very sparse, low-magnitude reset unit (max 0.039). It almost only fires in sequences of length 9 (97% of mass; a few in L=8, none in L<=7), and never during the original-input phase. Within those sequences it fires at the <DEL> step (t=9, about 26% of mass) and on the last three copy steps (recall_idx 6-8, t=15-17, about 71% of mass, peaking at the final two outputs). The predicate (L==9)&(t==9|t>=15) covers ~95% of activations and ~97% of mass, but precision is only ~0.5%: the unit fires on well under 1% of the steps in this context. Which ones it picks is only weakly tied to the input token, which is enriched for 0, f, n, 2, h (restricting to those tokens raises precision to ~3% but loses about 40% of mass). At <DEL> the strongest examples have f at original positions 1-2 (e.g. f f f..., 0 f f..., z f f...), but that does not generalize well (precision 3%). I found no clean rule for which steps get selected, and no magnitude modulator beyond later copy steps being more likely to fire.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues.
